alignments.note: Explicit subject pronoun takes only its own English word; the clause is verbless, so the supplied verbal frame goes to the predicate (rule 20).

The clause is verbless with a prepositional predicate, `בְּ` + `חֳלָיִים`; the ASV recasts it possessively as *shalt have*, so the preposition that makes the clause possessive carries the supplied *have* together with its modal auxiliary (rules 43 and 49), headed on *have*. No `הָיָה` and no existential particle stands in the clause. Competing reading: taking *shalt have* as rule 20's construction-supplied copula on `חֳלָיִים`; rejected because rule 43 assigns a *have* to the morpheme that makes the clause possessive, which here is the predicate preposition.
The predicate noun keeps its own English word; ASV's singular *sickness* for the Hebrew plural is a translation choice and does not affect the alignment.
Attributive adjective; the ASV fronts it before the noun.
Preposition rendered *by* (rule 11); its object `מַחֲלֵה` keeps its own English word, so the pair does not fuse under rule 30.
Construct noun takes only its own word; the chain's relational *of* belongs to the rectum (rule 19).
Nomen rectum of `מַחֲלֵה מֵעֶיךָ`, taking the chain's *of* with its own noun and headed on the noun (rules 19 and 24); discontinuous around the possessive under rule 25.
Pronominal suffix rendered by the possessive *thy* (rule 18).

Finite verb rendered by the phrasal verb *fall out*; the particle completes the lexeme of `יָצָא` and stays with the verb, headed on the lexical verb (rule 44). Discontinuous from its subject, which precedes it in the English.
Subject noun of the `עַד` clause, keeping its own word.
Pronominal suffix rendered by the possessive *thy* (rule 18).
Causal `מִן` rendered by the fixed English phrase *by reason of*, headed on the content word the phrase turns on rather than on either connective (rule 24).
First member of the distributive `יָמִים עַל־יָמִים`; each occurrence carries its own preposition-free English noun, so each morpheme takes the word written for it (rules 2 and 22).
`עַל` rendered by the distributive connective *by* standing between the two members (rule 11).
Second occurrence of `יָמִים`, rendered by the second *day*; nothing is left unrendered, so rule 22's unrepresented-occurrence sentence does not arise.

review_notes: The ASV marginal note *Or, year after year* was read and set aside; the printed text is what is aligned (rule 38).
`בָּחֳלָיִים` is preposition plus noun with no article morpheme segmented; the `בְּ` carries the recast *shalt have* under rules 43 and 49, and the noun keeps *sickness*.
Both `מֵעִים` occurrences and both `יָמִים` occurrences are rendered separately by the ASV, so no occurrence is marked unrepresented.
